articles.title: Nepal PM Urges Calm as Curfew Holds After Sectarian Clashes Kill Three
articles.excerpt: Several towns in southeastern Nepal remain under indefinite curfew after Hindu-Muslim violence erupted over a dispute involving loud music and religious flags during a Hindu event.
articles.nri_angle: Cross-border communities along the Nepal-India border face concerns about regional stability and safety of nationals in the area.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DR Congo's Ebola Death Toll Passes 1,500 as Outbreak Becomes Second-Largest on Record
articles.excerpt: With 3,532 confirmed cases and 1,556 deaths in less than three months, the DRC's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak now trails only the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic in scale.
articles.nri_angle: India, a major contributor to global health through WHO and African development partnerships, faces pressure to scale up support as the DRC Ebola crisis deepens; Indian pharmaceutical firms could also play a role in accelerating treatments for the rare Bundibugyo strain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 16 Indians Killed in Middle East Since February, Government Tells Parliament
articles.excerpt: India disclosed that ten merchant seafarers and six other nationals have died in the escalating US-Iran conflict, underscoring the risks facing over 300,000 Indian sailors worldwide.
articles.image_caption: India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar; the government told Parliament that 16 Indian nationals have been killed in the Middle East since February.
articles.nri_angle: Directly affects India's 300,000+ merchant seafarers and their families across coastal states; the disclosure raises questions about diaspora protection in conflict zones.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nirmal Purja and Nine Climbers Missing After Avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak
articles.excerpt: The record-breaking Nepalese mountaineer known for Netflix's '14 Peaks' led a 10-person expedition that has been out of contact since a snowslide struck around midday Thursday.
articles.nri_angle: Purja, who served with the British military's Brigade of Gurkhas, is a major figure in South Asian mountaineering; the missing team includes climbers from multiple nations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Denies Iran's Claims of Destroying F-35 Jets as Conflict Escalates
articles.excerpt: CENTCOM says all Iranian missiles were intercepted after IRGC claimed ballistic missile strikes destroyed American fighter jets at a Jordan air base, while the US and Saudi Arabia jointly struck Iran-backed groups in Iraq.
articles.nri_angle: Disruption to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which carried 20% of the world's oil, raises energy security concerns for India, which sources a significant share of its crude from the Persian Gulf.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran-Linked Hackers Suspected in Coordinated Attack on U.S. Water Systems
articles.excerpt: U.S. investigators point to Iranian-affiliated group CyberAv3ngers after more than 30 Minnesota water systems were targeted in cyberattacks that prompted a federal warning about escalating threats to critical infrastructure.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American communities concentrated in Minnesota's Twin Cities metro, home to a significant tech workforce, face the same water infrastructure vulnerabilities exposed by the attacks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Assam Floods Kill 75 as Entire Villages Vanish Across Upper Assam
articles.excerpt: A cloudburst in Nagaland triggered catastrophic flooding across seven districts, displacing over 3 lakh people and submerging more than 45,000 hectares of farmland in what residents call the worst deluge in living memory.
articles.nri_angle: The devastating Assam floods connect deeply with the Indian diaspora, many of whom have family in the affected Upper Assam districts and are watching the destruction of ancestral villages from abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Georgia School Shooter's Father Gets 15 Years in Landmark Sentencing
articles.excerpt: Colin Gray, the first U.S. parent convicted of murder for a child's school shooting, was sentenced Thursday after a judge told him he 'failed as a parent' by ignoring escalating warning signs.
articles.nri_angle: The case raises questions about gun safety and parental responsibility in the U.S., issues of particular concern for Indian-American families navigating school safety in their communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Salman Rushdie's Attacker Convicted of Federal Terrorism Charges, Faces Life in Prison
articles.excerpt: A jury needed just two hours to find Hadi Matar guilty of supporting Hezbollah and engaging in transnational terrorism over the 2022 stabbing of the Indian-born author.
articles.nri_angle: Rushdie, born in Mumbai to a Kashmiri Muslim family, is one of the most prominent literary figures of Indian origin; the case touches free expression and religious edict debates central to diaspora identity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Japan Earthquake Death Toll Climbs to 28 as Thousands Go Without Water in Sweltering Heat
articles.excerpt: Two days after the 7.1-magnitude quake struck Kumamoto, rescue operations continue at a destroyed mall and paper mill while heatstroke warnings mount.
articles.nri_angle: Over 56,000 Indians live in Japan, with communities near the affected zone; travel and safety advisories are relevant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Origin Woman, 26, Shot Dead in Targeted Attack in Toronto
articles.excerpt: Toronto police arrested 37-year-old Sharanjit Singh of Brampton and charged him with first-degree murder after Navneet Kaur was gunned down near Humberwood Boulevard. Her family alleges the accused had been harassing her after she rejected his marriage proposal.
articles.image_caption: Toronto police launched a search after a 26-year-old Indian-origin woman was fatally shot in the Rexdale neighbourhood on July 24.
articles.nri_angle: The killing adds to a growing list of violent deaths of Indian nationals in Canada, deepening anxiety among diaspora families and raising urgent questions about whether complaints of harassment and threats are being adequately addressed by Canadian authorities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bombay High Court Lets Gadkari Sue Meta, X, Google Over AI Deepfakes
articles.excerpt: The civil suit over fabricated videos linking the Union minister to the E20 fuel programme could become a landmark test of platform liability and personality rights in India.
articles.nri_angle: The case will test whether Indian courts can compel global tech platforms to act against AI-generated disinformation — a precedent relevant to diaspora members who rely on social media for news about Indian politics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CDC Issues Level 2 Travel Warning for Costa Rica Over Chikungunya Outbreak
articles.excerpt: The mosquito-borne virus is spreading locally in Costa Rica's popular Guanacaste Province, with India also listed among countries posing elevated risk for US travelers.
articles.nri_angle: India is listed among countries posing elevated chikungunya risk for US travelers, and Indian Americans traveling to either Costa Rica or India this summer should take precautions against mosquito bites.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SpaceX Falcon 9 Rocket Stage on Track to Crash Into the Moon on August 5
articles.excerpt: A spent upper stage from a 2025 lunar mission will slam into the surface near Einstein crater at 5,400 mph, creating a dust plume that astronomers worldwide plan to observe.
articles.nri_angle: The uncontrolled lunar impact underscores the growing space debris problem as India's ISRO prepares its own Chandrayaan-4 lunar sample return mission.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Indians Rescued in Thailand After Being Lured With Fake Tour Package and Held for Ransom
articles.excerpt: Five suspects arrested in Bangkok after the victims were tortured in a Pattaya house and their families asked to pay ₹40 lakh each, with the operation traced to a Pakistan-based mastermind in Dubai.
articles.nri_angle: Three young Indian men were kidnapped while traveling in Thailand, underscoring safety risks for Indian tourists abroad and the role of Indian embassies in coordinating rescues.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US and Saudi Arabia Launch First Joint Strikes on Iran-Backed Militias in Iraq, Killing at Least 20
articles.excerpt: The unprecedented operation targeted weapons and logistics sites across eastern Iraq after more than 30 drone attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure in 72 hours.
articles.nri_angle: Millions of Indians working in Gulf states face heightened security risks as the conflict escalates, while rising oil prices threaten India's import bill.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Signs Nuclear Deal With Saudi Arabia, Sparking Proliferation Fears Across the Middle East
articles.excerpt: The 30-year agreement could allow Riyadh to enrich uranium without the strictest international safeguards, drawing sharp criticism from arms control experts and some lawmakers.
articles.nri_angle: A nuclear-capable Saudi Arabia would reshape the geopolitical balance in a region home to millions of Indian workers and could trigger a wider Middle Eastern arms race.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Houthi Strikes Hit Saudi Aramco Facilities at Jizan and Yanbu as Red Sea Oil Route Comes Under Threat
articles.excerpt: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis attacked critical Saudi oil infrastructure along the Red Sea coast, sending shipping traffic to its lowest level in months.
articles.nri_angle: Attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure threaten energy prices globally and directly affect the millions of Indians living and working in Gulf states.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Claims 'Good Talks' With Iran but Threatens Strikes on Pickaxe Mountain if Deal Fails
articles.excerpt: The president said the U.S. has had productive discussions with Tehran while warning he would 'easily' destroy the fortified nuclear site if negotiations collapse.
articles.nri_angle: Escalation or de-escalation in the U.S.-Iran conflict directly affects oil prices, travel routes and geopolitical stability for the Indian diaspora across the Gulf.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Brushes Off Netanyahu's Opposition to F-35 Fighter Jet Sale to Turkey
articles.excerpt: As Netanyahu arrives in Washington for a high-stakes meeting, Trump declares 'nobody tells me what we should be selling' and calls Turkey a 'tremendous ally,' deepening a rift between the longtime partners.
articles.nri_angle: The potential F-35 sale to Turkey and shifting US alliances in the Middle East carry implications for India's own defense partnerships with Washington and regional security calculations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iranian Drones Strike Near US Consulate in Erbil as Conflict Enters Fragile Ceasefire
articles.excerpt: Multiple explosions rocked Iraq's Kurdish capital last week as Iran and the US exchange fire across the Middle East, with Trump now claiming 'good talks' with Tehran.
articles.nri_angle: 8 million Indians in Gulf states face safety concerns as conflict geography expands; Iraq is a major crude oil supplier to India
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Detects Omicron RF.5 Variant in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu as Officials Urge Calm
articles.excerpt: Genome sequencing confirms the new COVID-19 sub-lineage in samples from Kadapa district, but health authorities say current evidence shows no increased severity over existing Omicron strains.
articles.nri_angle: For Indians abroad planning travel or with elderly relatives in affected states, the current risk remains low with standard precautions advised and no travel advisories issued.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air India Begins Boeing 787 Modifications After FAA Flags Door Handle Detachment Risk
articles.excerpt: The airline is carrying out phased modifications to some of its 35 Dreamliners after the US aviation regulator issued an airworthiness directive over door assist handles that could pull loose during pre-flight checks.
articles.nri_angle: Air India's Dreamliner fleet serves major India-to-US and India-to-Europe routes heavily used by NRIs and diaspora travellers; safety compliance directly affects passenger confidence
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oil Tanker Explodes After Hitting Naval Mine in Strait of Hormuz as Iran Tightens Grip on Chokepoint
articles.excerpt: The blast on Sunday came as Iran's IRGC intercepted six more vessels and traffic through the world's most critical oil corridor has plunged 70% since the ceasefire collapsed.
articles.nri_angle: India sources roughly 60% of its crude oil from the Persian Gulf, making the Strait of Hormuz disruption a direct threat to fuel prices and energy security for the Indian economy and its diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bihar Arrests Cross 450 as Student Protest Deal Unravels Over FIR Withdrawals
articles.excerpt: Despite the Centre's agreement to drop cases against NEET protesters, Bihar police have detained over 450 people, prompting the Cockroach Janta Party to threaten fresh agitation and the Supreme Court to take up the matter.
articles.nri_angle: The protests, rooted in exam integrity and youth unemployment fears including AI displacement, resonate with diaspora families whose children face similar competitive pressures for Indian professional exams.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Killed, Teen Arrested in Mass Shooting at Seattle Food Festival
articles.excerpt: A 15-year-old suspect is in custody after gunfire at the annual Bite of Seattle festival near the Space Needle left three dead and four wounded, including a toddler.
articles.nri_angle: The shooting at a major Seattle summer festival hits close to home for the large Indian-American community in the greater Seattle-Bellevue tech corridor.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Supreme Court Justice Slams Arrests Over Chicken Biryani on the Ganga, Says 'Public Space for Dissent Is Shrinking'
articles.excerpt: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan cites the Varanasi Iftar case to warn that ordinary activities are being criminalised and courts are failing to protect fundamental freedoms.
articles.nri_angle: Supreme Court judge's remarks on shrinking space for dissent resonate with diaspora concerns about civil liberties in India
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ripudaman Singh Malik’s Killer Gets 15 More Years for Separate Abbotsford Manslaughter
articles.excerpt: Tanner Fox, already serving life for the assassination of the former Air India bombing suspect, pleaded guilty to the 2022 killing of Chad Colivas in an unrelated break-in gone wrong.
articles.image_caption: An Air India Boeing 747 on the tarmac at Frankfurt Airport. The 1985 bombing of Air India Flight 182 killed 329 people and remains the deadliest act of aviation terrorism in Canadian history.
articles.nri_angle: The 1985 Air India bombing and Malik’s subsequent acquittal remain pivotal events for the Indian and Sikh diaspora in Canada, and the unresolved question of who ordered his assassination continues to unsettle communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FDA Approves First OTC Pill Combining Tylenol and Naproxen for 12-Hour Pain Relief
articles.excerpt: The first-ever fixed-dose over-the-counter combination of acetaminophen and naproxen sodium offers up to 12 hours of non-opioid pain relief for adults and children 12 and older.
articles.nri_angle: The approval introduces a convenient single-pill pain relief option combining acetaminophen (known as paracetamol in India) with naproxen, relevant to Indian-Americans managing chronic pain conditions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Orders Warning Signs Outside Smithsonian Over 'Inaccurate' History Exhibits
articles.excerpt: The executive order directs the National Park Service to install signage near the National Museum of American History, escalating a culture war over how the country tells its own story.
articles.nri_angle: The Smithsonian's Indian and South Asian collections, including exhibits on immigration and cultural contributions, could be affected by the administration's push to reshape museum narratives.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Returns to White House Correspondents' Dinner Three Months After Assassination Attempt
articles.excerpt: The rescheduled event moves to a smaller venue with heightened security after a gunman stormed the April gala, forcing evacuations and leaving a Secret Service officer wounded.
articles.nri_angle: The rescheduled dinner underscored First Amendment protections and press freedom debates relevant to all Americans, including Indian Americans working in media and politics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SCOTUSblog Founder Tom Goldstein Sentenced to Six Years for Tax Evasion
articles.excerpt: The once-prominent Supreme Court litigator was convicted on 12 felony counts tied to millions in hidden poker winnings, offshore accounts, and mortgage fraud.
articles.nri_angle: The case highlights the scrutiny facing high-profile professionals in the U.S. legal system, resonating with Indian-American attorneys and finance professionals navigating complex tax obligations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Weighs 'Massive' Iran Escalation as War Enters Critical Phase
articles.excerpt: The US president says he is close to ordering the largest strike yet against Iran, even as back-channel talks gain traction through Pakistan and China.
articles.nri_angle: Sustained oil price spikes from the Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb disruptions threaten India's energy costs and the livelihoods of millions of Indian workers in the Gulf, while Pakistan's emergence as a mediator adds a South Asian dimension to the conflict.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: China Brokers Pakistan-Iran Channel to Restart Diplomacy With Washington
articles.excerpt: Beijing is quietly facilitating a three-way diplomatic push as Pakistan and Iran seek separate paths back to negotiations with the US amid the Gulf conflict.
articles.nri_angle: 8 million Indians in the Gulf; Chabahar port investment; energy security stakes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Barack Obama Surprises WNBA All-Stars at Presidential Center Practice
articles.excerpt: The former president walked onto the court before Friday's practice in Chicago, praising players for elevating women's basketball and chatting with Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese.
articles.nri_angle: The Obama Presidential Center is the first professional sports venue on Chicago's South Side, a neighborhood with a significant South Asian business community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Activist Sonam Wangchuk Ends 26-Day Hunger Strike as India's 'Cockroach' Protest Movement Intensifies
articles.excerpt: The 59-year-old Ladakhi activist broke his fast after government ministers visited him in hospital, but the youth-led movement demanding the education minister's resignation shows no sign of stopping.
articles.nri_angle: The Cockroach movement has drawn global attention to India's competitive exam crisis, which directly shapes the pipeline of Indian students seeking US university spots and eventually H-1B visas.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Thirteen Killed Including Infant as Landslide Crushes Taxi in Himachal Pradesh's Lahaul-Spiti
articles.excerpt: The passengers had been stranded overnight after an earlier landslide blocked the road and were resuming their journey to Pangi Valley when boulders struck their vehicle.
articles.nri_angle: Himachal Pradesh is a popular tourist destination for NRIs visiting India; the monsoon-season landslide toll raises questions about road safety in the Himalayas.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ICC Members Vote to Dismiss Prosecutor Karim Khan Over Sexual Misconduct Allegations
articles.excerpt: Eighty-two of the International Criminal Court's 125 member states voted to remove the British-Pakistani barrister in a secret ballot at UN headquarters in New York.
articles.nri_angle: Khan, born in Edinburgh to a Pakistani dermatologist father, is one of the most prominent British-South Asian legal figures on the world stage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
